chunks: And Abān narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who said, “A camel is due from me,” but did not specify where he would slaughter it, he عليه السلام said: “Slaughtering is only at Minā, and he should distribute it among the needy.”

key_terms.النَّحْرُ: the ritual slaughter of the sacrificial camel
key_terms.الْمَسَاكِينِ: the needy people among whom the meat is to be distributed
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: a camel designated as a sacrificial offering
key_terms.بِمِنًى: at Minā, the designated place mentioned in this ruling

ai.seo_question: If someone vows to offer a camel without specifying where it should be slaughtered, where must it be slaughtered and to whom is it distributed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a vowed camel sacrifice when the person did not specify the place of slaughter. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that it is to be slaughtered at Minā and distributed among the needy, indicating both the proper location and charitable disposition of the offering.
